issues.display_title: Issue #117: Stamp created_at on canvas objects (server-authoritative) + backfill migration
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Backend half of FE GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#392 (editor object list must sort newest→oldest instead of grouping by type). Decided approach: Option C — server-authoritative created_at.

Context

The editor object list currently groups by type because there is no per-object creation order anywhere. FE stamps a provisional created_at (epoch ms) on each object as it is created; the backend canonicalizes it so ordering is consistent across clients and survives blob round-trips.

The canvas is stored as an opaque blob (canvas_data / the floorplan payload) — today neither the API nor the socket parses objects. This task introduces that parsing on the API side only. The socket (gothru-maps-socket) needs no change: edit.handler.ts relays an opaque snapshot string, so created_at rides inside it automatically.

Scope

  • On project save (canvas/floorplan blob write), parse the level objects per type and assign a monotonic created_at to any object lacking one, keyed by object id:
    • layout.walls[], layout.areas[]
    • floorplanMeta.doors[], floorplanMeta.windows[] (⚠️ these carry no id — key by array index within the level, or agree an id with FE)
    • shapes[], points[], safetyAnnotations[], panoramas[]
  • Never overwrite an existing created_at (FE's provisional value wins; server only fills gaps and normalizes).
  • Write the enriched blob back so the value persists.
  • Migration: backfill created_at for existing projects' blobs. Legacy objects have no historical timestamp anywhere, so order is best-effort (type-traversal); old projects can't be made exact — documented limitation, same for any approach.

Caveats to keep in mind

  • Schema coupling: the parser now depends on the FE object schema. Any new object type/field on FE must be mirrored here. Keep one shared shape doc.
  • Collab edge case: objects created during a live collab session sync via the socket without hitting an API save, so they carry only the FE-provisional created_at until the next persist. That is by design (hybrid) — the server just canonicalizes later.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Saving a project stamps created_at on every object that lacks one; existing values are untouched.
  • Objects round-trip through save/load with created_at preserved.
  • Migration backfills existing projects without corrupting blobs (dry-run/verify first).
  • go build ./... and go test ./... green (predict tests may fail on sandbox /tmp perms — pre-existing).

RESULT

Shipped in PR #118 (commit 24a9f38), merged to development.

  • shared.StampCanvasCreatedAt walks canvas_data as generic JSON (json.Decoder + UseNumber, so coordinates and ids re-encode byte-identical) over a list of known object array paths: layout.walls, layout.areas, floorplanMeta.doors, floorplanMeta.windows, shapes, points, safetyAnnotations, panoramas. Deliberately not a mirror of the FE structs — unknown/new fields round-trip untouched, and only a brand-new object array needs a line here. That keeps the FE↔BE coupling to a path list instead of a schema copy.
  • Wired into both canvas writers: project.Update and floorplan.Post.
  • A missing createdAt means "unknown", not "now". The client stamps objects as it sees them created, so anything arriving unstamped predates the field; it gets unknownCreatedAt (the oldest stamp). Backfilling with the current clock would sort every untouched legacy object above the one the user just drew — the bug this feature exists to fix.
  • Existing values are never overwritten; an unparsable or unexpected blob is returned unchanged so a save can never fail on it.

Migration deliberately skipped. With the sentinel design, a standalone backfill writes the same "oldest" marker the next save writes anyway, and the FE already treats an absent value as oldest — so it changes no ordering for any project. Legacy objects have no historical creation time to recover in the first place. Reopen if we later want the field materialized eagerly for reporting.

Socket (gothru-maps-socket): no change — edit.handler.ts relays an opaque snapshot string, so createdAt rides inside it.

go build ./... green; go test ./... green except the pre-existing predict sandbox /tmp permission failures.
